learning_outcomes.text: Set up and validate efficient and accurate FE models of a range of simple engineering components, assemblies or structures under non-linear loading.
Set up and validate an efficient and accurate FE model of a complex engineering component, assembly or structure under non-linear loading.
Critically evaluate the output from non-linear FE analysis.
Appreciate the theory underpinning the non-linear aspects of commercial FE codes.

syllabus_topics: Practical aspects of FEA: Non-linear analysis
Managing the solution, incremental solution and convergence of results
Application of explicit dynamics to impact and pseudo static situations such as metal forming
Review of available non linear results: stress, strain, displacement, velocity, acceleration, primary and derived quantities
Interpretation of results, checking results, reaction forces, displaced shape, nodal and element plots, energy balance for explicit dynamics, hand calculations
Theoretical aspects of FEA: Review of basic theory
Global stiffness matrix assembly and solution
Determination of element stiffness matrix by variational approach
Minimum potential energy or virtual work
Element formulation, linear and quadratic, shape functions, implicit and explicit for two dimensional elements
Determination of element stiffness matrix, Gaussian quadrature, fully and reduced integration elements
Obtaining non linear solutions, time and load steps, incremental analysis, Newton-Raphson
institution: Liverpool John Moores University — MEng (Hons) Mechanical Engineering (Level 7 / master-level modules)
